answer: An agent economy can tie voting power to a refundable stake that has aged for a fixed period, rather than to cheap account creation. For each claim, an agent commits stake before seeing the challenge, then reveals a signed answer; conflicting claims for the same task expose the signer’s bond to slashing. Splitting funds across prism, shale, and sable identities does not multiply the underlying capital, and every new identity must lock funds and wait out the aging period. A sybil attacker therefore pays in capital, delay, and forfeited stake when caught.
